title: Unicode Standard 17.0.0, Chapter 16: South and Southeast Asian Scripts — Khmer
scope: Khmer encoding structure, consonant registers, coeng, vowel signs, independent vowels, signs, visual/logical order

title: Richard Ishida, Khmer (Cambodian) Orthography Notes
scope: Modern Khmer orthography, consonant registers, vowel-sign behavior, IPA-oriented descriptive phonology, syllable structure

title: The Standard Khmer vowel system: An acoustic study
scope: Phnom Penh acoustic vowel system; 21 source-reported monophthongs and 13 diphthongs; class/register and coda effects
method: 21 speakers screened with 168 items; four speakers (two female) selected for acoustic analysis; 61 lexical items, three formal-reading repetitions
limitations: No exhaustive consonant-series × vowel × coda cross-table; /i/ omitted from acoustic sample; Standard Khmer and Phnom Penh contrasts differ; source transcription is not project gold

title: The Main features of Cambodian Pronunciation
journal: Bulletin of the School of Oriental and African Studies 14(1):149–174
scope: historically important description of Khmer register and pronunciation

title: Incipient tonogenesis in Phnom Penh Khmer: Acoustic and perceptual studies
scope: Phnom Penh production and perception; f0, aspiration/VOT, voice quality and vowel-quality cues associated with colloquial /r/-loss

title: Incipient tonogenesis in Phnom Penh Khmer: Computational studies
scope: phonologization of f0 and breathy phonation following /r/-loss

title: Sound changes following the loss of /r/ in Khmer: a new tonogenetic mechanism?
scope: Phnom Penh colloquial /Cr/ forms vs careful reading; two male speakers, 20 lexical items, three repetitions per style; VOT/frication, F0 at five vowel positions and F1/F2; not a universal deletion rule

title: Transliteration of Khmer Writing
scope: comparison of Khmer romanization systems and orthographic flexibility

title: Khmer-Russian practical transcription
scope: Russian practical treatment of Khmer vowels, consonants, aspiration, clusters and glottal stop
note: Secondary web reproduction citing the 1967 Cambodian geographic-name instructions, Gorgoniyev and Serdyuchenko. Use as comparator until primary scans are independently verified.

title: Fourth International Linguistics Olympiad, Individual Problems, Problem 3
scope: Bulgarian-language academic material containing Latin phonetic transcription of Khmer data

title: MekongPhon: A Large-Scale Parallel IPA Corpus for Lao and Khmer
scope: Paper reports 1,314,779 Khmer orthography–IPA sentence pairs; seed lexicon has 8,026 word–IPA entries derived from Headley (1977), with a two-author 500-entry review (99.2% sample accuracy; reviewers are proficient L2 speakers, not native speakers). Sentence pairs are generated by longest-match trie lookup over OPUS text (NLLB/Paracrawl/OpenSubtitles); held-out evaluation is dictionary-seeded and reports <2% CER under the paper's own setup, not independent sentence transcription or our gold. Candidate secondary lexical reference/diagnostic only; not blind adjudicated IPA gold. Repository snapshot f80f6c1840c4818b51e05f2e00cded4701a5b662 has no declared license/root LICENSE; SEALang license version unspecified; rights_status=UNKNOWN pending item-level verification.

title: Applying Linguistic G2P Knowledge on a Statistical Grapheme-to-phoneme Conversion in Khmer
scope: prose reports 1,350 training pairs and 350 test pairs, but Table 10 test-corpus bins sum to 356 (112+97+98+49); abstract baseline WER 69.6% conflicts with Table 10/conclusion 69.9%; preserve discrepancies pending author clarification; dataset/normalization/profile need recovery before comparison
article_license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (article only; not a statement of source-dictionary or derived-data rights)

title: Incipient tonogenesis in Phnom Penh Khmer: audio recordings, 2011
author: James Kirby
scope: 24-bit, 44.1 kHz audio of 16 Phnom Penh Khmer speakers recorded in July 2011, with segmented Praat TextGrids; the associated study contrasts reading and colloquial /CrV/ productions
limitations: Not a lexical-wide IPA gold corpus; TextGrids provide segmentation rather than independent IPA labels; the study targets /CrV/ contexts and a historical speaker sample, not the complete contemporary citation-form lexicon. Keep reading and colloquial conditions separate.

title: Incipient tonogenesis in Phnom Penh Khmer: supplementary materials, 2011
author: James Kirby
scope: Anonymised production and perception CSVs, KlattGrid stimulus files, Praat-related measurements and R analysis code accompanying the Phnom Penh /r/-loss study
limitations: Not a lexical IPA gold corpus and not a complete phonetic transcription dataset; CSVs are study measurements/response data, not independently double-annotated IPA. Interpret only within the source study's task and speaker scope.

title: Assessing transcription agreement: Methodological aspects
author: Catia Cucchiarini
scope: Critique of percentage agreement for phonetic transcription: all-or-none symbol matching, chance agreement and missing alignment criteria; proposes alignment and average distance using experimentally derived phonetic feature matrices
limitations: Not a Khmer-specific annotation standard or universal weight matrix; informs reporting and metric design but does not supply validated Khmer feature weights.

title: A Weighted Reliability Measure for Phonetic Transcription
journal: Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research 49(6):1391–1411
scope: Weighted reliability measure for phonetic transcription, designed to distinguish degrees of phonetic difference using principles from phonological theory; evaluated with eight coders on speech and vocalisation samples, including three adult languages
limitations: Not a language-specific Khmer feature matrix; the project's current validator does not implement this published measure. A future project metric must not be attributed to Oller and Ramsdell unless their exact algorithm is reproduced.

title: Procesy fonetyczno-fonologiczne w nieregionalnej odmianie języka khmerskiego
author: Piotr Woźnica
scope: Acoustic study of 80 native Khmer speakers from multiple Cambodian regions; examines regional phonetic/phonological variation and argues for a country-wide standard variety
limitations: The thesis warns that the sample is not statistically representative; regional coverage is uneven and the materials are selective/read-text based. It is not a Phnom Penh-only sample or a lexical IPA gold corpus.

title: Khmer ASR Cultural Dataset, Version 3 Part 1
author: Digital Divide Data (DDD-Cambodia)
scope: 134.60 hours of manually curated Khmer speech-text recordings; Part 1 metadata reports 8 Cambodia-based native speakers (4 female, 4 male), 13 topics and 401 subtopics; speaker origin-city metadata is provided. WAV audio and orthographic transcripts; CC BY-SA 4.0; attribution to Digital Divide Data required.
limitations: No IPA labels or phonetic adjudication are supplied. Speaker origin city does not by itself establish a Phnom Penh phonological profile. Use only after selecting profile and filtering speaker/recording metadata; preserve utterance and word-span locators; do not attempt speaker identification. Share-alike obligations and redistribution of any derived IPA must be reviewed before publication.

title: Common Voice Scripted Speech 27.0 — Khmer
author: Mozilla Common Voice
scope: CC0-1.0 read-speech audio; 739 clips / 0.98h total, 213 validated clips / 0.28h validated, 15 speakers, 4,971 text sentences; only 364 sentences validated. Accent values absent for the reported subset; gender unreported for all speakers. Provider forbids speaker identification and re-hosting/re-sharing.
limitations: No IPA labels. Accent/variety is not established, so the data cannot be assumed to represent Phnom Penh or Standard Khmer. Most clips are unresolved/invalidated (483 unresolved, 43 invalidated); only 213 are validated. Use provider-hosted audio and opaque clip/time locators only; do not identify speakers or mirror/re-share files. Specialist profile screening and blind double annotation/adjudication remain required.

title: open-dict-data/ipa-dict — Khmer km.txt
scope: 3,286-line Khmer orthography-to-IPA lexicon in tab-separated format. Repository README attributes Khmer data to extraction from the Khmer-English Dictionary at aakanee.com.
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 for the third-party Khmer data as identified in the upstream Credits; repository-wide MIT license does not override third-party data terms.
limitations: Not project gold or independent double annotation. Exact dialect/profile, transcription convention, source entry locators, and duplicate/alternative-reading handling require further review. Non-commercial/share-alike terms make this unsuitable for an unrestricted commercial release. Do not import or redistribute until compatibility with project purpose and obligations is reviewed.

title: PhonSobon Khmer G2P — Khmer Dictionary 2022 derived word-to-pronunciation pairs
scope: 38,629 word-to-pronunciation pairs (37,755 unique words) with 34,770 train, 1,939 validation and 1,920 test rows; word-level split groups all readings of a word. Pronunciation is NCKL Khmer-script respelling with syllable boundaries, not IPA. Derived from the Khmer Dictionary 2022 of the National Council of Khmer Language, Royal Academy of Cambodia.
limitations: Useful as a structural/syllabification research comparator only after rights and profile review. The dataset card says source content remains © NCKL and commercial terms must be checked; no independent open redistribution permission is established by the dataset card. Cleaning includes removed rows and source corrections. Do not treat as IPA gold, import as pronunciation gold, or infer IPA mechanically.

title: PhonSobon Khmer pronunciation dictionary (combined)
scope: 39,110 Khmer word-to-pronunciation-respelling rows; combined from Khmer Dictionary 2022-derived sources. Dataset card documents 689 disputed words with review decisions (650 judge decisions and 39 Claude-assisted confirmations requiring native-speaker confirmation).
limitations: Not IPA. Review provenance includes automated/LLM-assisted decisions and explicitly calls for native-speaker confirmation; not independent expert IPA adjudication. Source content is stated as research-only/non-commercial; do not import into a commercial or redistributable gold corpus without permission and source-level rights review.

title: Khmer Acoustic Model for Montreal Forced Aligner
scope: Upstream README claims 29,204 IPA dictionary entries validated by native Khmer linguists and declares CC BY-SA 4.0 for the pronunciation dictionary. The repository tree exposes only a six-line sample dictionary, not the claimed full dictionary. The dictionary README separately declares CC BY 4.0 for a mapping derived from 33,091 entries; artifact counts and data-license statements are not reconciled.
license: Unresolved: root README says CC BY-SA 4.0 for pronunciation dictionary; dictionary README says CC BY 4.0 for a G2P mapping; code LICENSE is MIT but does not resolve third-party data terms.
limitations: Do not import sample or claim full dictionary access. Request versioned full artifact and SHA-256, artifact-specific licenses, provenance, dialect/IPA convention, annotation/adjudication details, and release/DOI. Alignment boundary metrics are not phonetic accuracy.

title: BYU MATRIX Lab Khmer IPA model
scope: 33.6M-parameter BERT encoder-decoder with separate Khmer and IPA tokenizers; model card reports best evaluation loss 0.1736 at checkpoint 26000; the model card's example output is IPA-like. The LREC 2026 MekongPhon paper reports under 2% CER on its own held-out evaluation setup.
license: Apache-2.0 as declared by the model card
limitations: The model card license does not resolve rights in the training corpus; MekongPhon repository snapshot has no declared root LICENSE. Source-attested diagnostic results are not independent project gold; model evaluation uses pron_no_tones and does not establish tone/phonation recovery.

title: PhonSobon Khmer G2P (NCKL respelling)
scope: 7.46M-parameter character-level Transformer predicts NCKL Khmer-script respelling with hyphenated syllable boundaries; model card reports 83.37% validation word accuracy at epoch 150.
license: MIT as declared by model card
limitations: Output is Khmer-script respelling, not IPA; no test score is reported in the model card. The separate training dataset derives from the NCKL Khmer Dictionary 2022 and its dataset card asks users to check NCKL terms before commercial use.

title: PhonSobon Khmer G2P dataset (derived from NCKL Khmer Dictionary 2022)
scope: 38,629 word-to-pronunciation pairs and 37,755 unique words; train 34,770, validation 1,939, test 1,920; word-level split keeps all readings of a word together. Labels are Khmer-script respellings with hyphenated syllable boundaries, not IPA.
limitations: Standard NCKL/Phnom Penh prescribed word pronunciations; not regional/colloquial variants and not running-speech sandhi. Dataset card attributes content to NCKL and explicitly advises checking NCKL terms before commercial use; do not redistribute/use commercially without rights clarification.
